questions.solution: Correct option: B. Paris (2015) is an agreement under the UNFCCC. NDCs are nationally determined; Kyoto was the earlier protocol with annex-based targets.

questions.q: The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was primarily concerned with:
options: Indigo planters’ tinkathia system in Bihar
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Gandhi’s first satyagraha in India targeted forced indigo cultivation. It is a BPSC/UPSC favourite bridge between modern India and Bihar.

questions.q: El Niño is best described as:
options: A permanent cold current off Peru
A periodic warming of the central/eastern equatorial Pacific that can disturb Indian monsoon probabilities
A type of cyclone in the Bay of Bengal only
questions.solution: Correct option: B. ENSO is a coupled ocean–atmosphere oscillation. El Niño raises the chance of a weak monsoon; it is not a guarantee of drought everywhere.

questions.q: NavIC is:
options: A river-linking canal in north Bihar
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Navigation with Indian Constellation is ISRO’s regional GNSS. Map it to applications (timing, disaster, transport), not only satellite nicknames.

questions.q: A Money Bill under Article 110 can be introduced only in:
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Money Bills originate in the Lok Sabha on the President’s recommendation. Rajya Sabha can only recommend; it cannot reject.

questions.q: Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance under a convention signed at:
questions.solution: Correct option: B. The Ramsar Convention (1971) lists wetlands. India has many Ganga-basin sites relevant to Bihar/UP floodplain ecology.

papers.note: Selected official-style 2023 GS items with solutions.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission: 1. It is a constitutional body. 2. It recommends distribution of tax proceeds between Union and States. Which is/are correct?
questions.solution: Correct option: C. Article 280 creates the Finance Commission. Vertical and horizontal devolution, plus grants, are its core. GST Council is a different federal body.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are listed as Fundamental Duties in Article 51A?
options: To safeguard public property and abjure violence
questions.solution: Correct option: B. 51A includes respect for the Constitution, composite culture, environment, scientific temper, public property, and education of children (86th Amendment), among others.

questions.q: The ‘ring of fire’ is associated with:
options: Circum-Pacific plate boundaries with volcanoes and earthquakes
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Convergent Pacific margins explain most of the world’s stratovolcanoes and great earthquakes.

questions.q: The Cabinet Mission (1946) proposed:
options: Immediate Partition into two dominions only
A three-tier federal structure and a Constituent Assembly
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Cabinet Mission rejected Pakistan as then demanded, suggested groups of provinces, and a Constituent Assembly — the hinge into Constitution-making.

questions.q: Core inflation typically excludes:
options: Food and fuel prices that are very volatile
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Core CPI is headline inflation minus food and energy so that MPC can see underlying demand pressure.

questions.q: In-situ conservation refers to:
options: Protecting species in their natural habitat (national parks, sanctuaries)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. National parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves are in-situ. Ex-situ is zoos, gene banks, botanic gardens.

questions.q: mRNA vaccines work primarily by:
options: Inserting a live virus that always causes disease
Instructing cells to make an antigen so adaptive immunity is trained
questions.solution: Correct option: B. A short-lived mRNA template produces spike (or other) protein; it does not alter DNA.

questions.q: The basic structure doctrine was laid down in:
options: Golaknath only, with no later case
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Parliament may amend under 368 but cannot destroy basic structure. Later cases applied it to Ninth Schedule, NJAC, etc.

questions.q: Attorney-General of India: which is correct?
options: He has the right to speak in Parliament but not to vote
He is appointed by the CJI
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Article 76: the AG is the Union’s lawyer, enjoys audience in all courts, and may participate in Parliament without a vote.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Constitutional body?
questions.solution: Correct option: B. ECI is in Part XV. NITI is executive; NGT and SEBI are statutory.

questions.q: La Niña is generally associated with:
options: Cooler than average eastern equatorial Pacific, often boosting Indian monsoon chances
questions.solution: Correct option: B. La Niña is the cold phase of ENSO. Treat it as a probability shifter, not a rainfall guarantee.

questions.q: Who among the following organised the Home Rule Movement in India?
options: Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak (among others)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Home Rule Leagues (1916) demanded self-government within the Empire and revived Extremists after 1907.

questions.q: GST in India is best described as:
options: A destination-based dual indirect tax levied by Union and States
A customs duty on services only
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Dual GST (CGST+SGST) or IGST on inter-State supply; GST Council is the federal bargain.

questions.q: PM2.5 refers to:
options: Fine particulate matter that can enter deep into the lungs
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Particles ≤2.5 μm drive NCAP and AQI debates. Pair with sources: vehicles, biomass, industry, dust.

questions.q: Web 3.0 discussions in GS often involve:
options: Decentralised protocols, digital public infrastructure and data rights
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Write application + regulation (data protection, cyber) + inclusion, not jargon.

questions.q: Anti-defection law is in:
questions.solution: Correct option: B. 52nd Amendment; 91st tweaked. Speaker/Chair decides; courts have reviewed the process (Kihoto, later cases).

questions.q: Right to Property in India today is:
options: A Fundamental Right in Part III
A constitutional legal right under Article 300A
questions.solution: Correct option: B. 44th Amendment removed 19(1)(f)/31 from FRs. 300A still requires authority of law to deprive a person of property.

questions.q: The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) allocated to India the use of:
options: The eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) with specified rights on the western rivers
questions.solution: Correct option: B. World Bank-brokered treaty. Western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) are largely for Pakistan with Indian limited uses.

questions.q: Fiscal deficit is:
options: Government’s total expenditure minus total receipts except borrowings
questions.solution: Correct option: B. It is the borrowing requirement. Revenue deficit and primary deficit are related but not identical.

questions.q: Black cotton soils (regur) in India are mainly associated with:
options: Deccan trap / basalt regions, good for cotton
Pure desert sand of Jaisalmer only
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Weathered basalt, moisture-retentive, cracks in summer. Contrast with alluvium of the Ganga plain.

questions.q: The Montreal Protocol is aimed at:
questions.solution: Correct option: B. ODS (CFCs etc.). Kigali Amendment later added HFCs (climate, not ozone). Do not mix with UNFCCC.

questions.q: CRISPR is:
options: A genome-editing tool with agriculture/health uses and biosafety issues
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Write GEAC/ethics/IPR beside the mechanism.

questions.q: Which House is called a permanent House?
questions.solution: Correct option: B. One-third of Rajya Sabha retires every two years; it is not subject to dissolution like Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi was first called ‘Father of the Nation’ in a public political context most famously associated with:
options: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s radio address from abroad (among popular attributions)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. The popular attribution is Bose, 1944. UPSC may still prefer a careful ‘often attributed’ framing in Mains.

questions.q: Rajya Sabha has exclusive power to:
options: Impeach the President alone without Lok Sabha
Pass a resolution to create an All-India Service (Article 312)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Special powers: 249 (Rajya Sabha can authorise Parliament to legislate on a State List matter in national interest) and 312.

questions.q: The Atal Tunnel is associated with:
options: Connecting the mainland to Sri Lanka
Rohtang / Manali–Lahaul access, all-weather road to the Himalayan interior
questions.solution: Correct option: B. High-altitude highway tunnel; disaster and logistics geography for Himachal–Ladakh access.

questions.q: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for:
options: Provincial autonomy and a proposed All-India Federation (which never fully came into being)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Provincial autonomy from 1937; Centre remained constrained. It heavily influenced the 1950 Constitution’s federal lists.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of SEBI?
options: Regulate the securities market and protect investors
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Statutory regulator. RBI is monetary/banking; CBDT is direct tax.

questions.q: Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) belong to:
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Each party files NDCs; India has energy-intensity, non-fossil capacity and sink-related pledges that evolve over cycles.

questions.q: Fifth-generation fighter aircraft are generally characterised by:
options: Stealth, sensor fusion and supermaneuverability (among other traits)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Tejas Mk-1 is not fifth generation; do not confuse with Rafale/Su-30 class either.

questions.q: Preamble to the Indian Constitution declares India to be:
options: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic (after 42nd Amendment words)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. 42nd Amendment inserted Socialist and Secular. Kesavananda treated Preamble as a key to basic structure.

questions.q: Western Disturbances affecting north India in winter originate over:
options: The Mediterranean / West Asian region and travel east in the westerlies
El Niño directly as a cyclone in Odisha
The Equator as trade winds only
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Extra-tropical systems that bring winter rain/snow to NW India and sometimes Bihar’s western fringe.

questions.q: Which Article is the principal home of the right to marry a person of one’s choice, as read by the Supreme Court in the Hadiya matter?
options: Article 14 only, with no liberty clause
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Liberty under 21 includes choice in marriage, subject to valid law. Pair with Puttaswamy (privacy).

questions.q: The term ‘Ahrar’ and ‘Rihai’ in the context of Indian national movement are associated with:
options: Khilafat / Muslim political currents of the early 20th century
questions.solution: Correct option: B. UPSC often pulls lesser-known organisational names from modern India — revise Spectrum’s organisations lists.

questions.q: Which of the following is issued by a commercial bank?
options: Treasury bills of the Government of India as owner
Sovereign gold bonds as issuer of last resort
questions.solution: Correct option: B. CDs are negotiable money-market instruments issued by banks. T-bills are government paper.

questions.q: Which of the following are in the IUCN Red List categories?
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Prelims loves the ladder: LC, NT, VU, EN, CR, EW, EX.

questions.q: The Strait of Hormuz is strategically important because it:
options: Links the Mediterranean to the Black Sea
Is a chokepoint for Persian Gulf oil to the open ocean
questions.solution: Correct option: B. IR + geography: energy security and naval presence.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General is correct?
options: CAG is appointed by the Prime Minister alone without the President
CAG audits government accounts and reports to the President who lays them in Parliament
CAG sits in the Union Cabinet
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Articles 148–151. Independence is a basic-structure flavour issue in Mains.

questions.q: Digital Public Infrastructure in India is illustrated by:
options: Aadhaar, UPI and related India Stack building blocks
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Inclusion plus exclusion errors, consent and cyber risk belong in the same note.

questions.q: The Battle of Plassey (1757) is important because it:
options: Opened Bengal to Company political power after a palace conspiracy and military clash
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Follow with Buxar (1764) and Diwani (1765) for the Company-as-state story.

questions.q: Which of the following are the core organs of the United Nations?
options: General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Secretariat, ICJ (and Trusteeship Council still listed)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Six organs in the Charter; Trusteeship is inactive. Prelims still asks the list.

questions.q: The Supreme Court’s judgement in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) vs Union of India is related to:
options: Right to privacy as a Fundamental Right
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Nine-judge Bench, 2017: privacy in 14/19/21. Foundation for Aadhaar, data protection and later cases.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes ‘inclusive growth’?
options: Growth that expands income with equity in jobs, health and education
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Survey language: employment, social sector, regional balance — not GDP alone.

questions.q: The ‘Bio-diversity Act’ of India was enacted in:
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Biological Diversity Act, 2002 implements CBD: NBA, SBBs, BMCs, ABS.

questions.q: Which of the following is a west-flowing river of the Peninsula?
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Narmada and Tapi flow west in rift valleys. Most large peninsular rivers drain east to the Bay.

questions.q: The well-known painting ‘Bani Thani’ belongs to the:
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Culture Prelims: school + region + patron. Kishangarh’s elongated lyrical style.

questions.q: ‘3D printing’ has applications in:
options: Prototyping, medical implants and selected manufacturing, with IP and safety issues
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Additive manufacturing: GS-III industry + S&T.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a Fundamental Right in India?
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Property is 300A, not Part III, after the 44th Amendment.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission is correct?
options: It is a constitutional body that superintends elections to Parliament, State legislatures and the offices of President and VP
It conducts panchayat elections in every State by itself
It is headed by the Law Minister
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Article 324. Local body elections are with State Election Commissions (73rd/74th).

questions.q: Which of the following is/are tributaries of the Brahmaputra?
questions.solution: Correct option: B. NE drainage is a Prelims map staple. In Bangladesh it becomes Jamuna.

questions.q: The ‘Swadeshi Movement’ is most closely associated with the partition of:
questions.solution: Correct option: B. 1905 Partition → Swadeshi and boycott, Extremists vs Moderates, later 1911 reunification.

questions.q: Which of the following is the function of the RBI?
options: Banker to the government and manager of foreign exchange (among other functions)
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Monetary authority, issuer of currency, banker to banks, public debt manager, forex.

questions.q: The term ‘Domestic Content Requirement’ is sometimes seen in the news in the context of:
options: Inducing locally manufactured solar equipment / WTO disputes
questions.solution: Correct option: A. India–US solar WTO dispute is the classic GS-III hook.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are famous for Sun temples?
options: Only Nalanda mahavihara as a sun temple
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Culture map: Konark (Odisha), Modhera (Gujarat), Martand (Kashmir, ruins).

questions.q: Democracy’s most essential feature is:
options: Free and fair elections with one person one vote, plus rule of law
questions.solution: Correct option: B. NCERT Democratic Politics: elections are necessary but not sufficient — rights and accountability complete it.

questions.q: Mediterranean climate is characterised by:
options: Rain throughout the year like equatorial rainforest
questions.solution: Correct option: B. West coasts ~30–40°: California, central Chile, Cape, SW Australia, Mediterranean basin.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are among the Fundamental Duties of citizens?
options: To vote in every election mandatorily under the Constitution
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To pay income tax as a Fundamental Duty listed in 51A word for word as ‘GST’
questions.solution: Correct option: B. 51A(c) and neighbouring clauses. Voting is a statutory/constitutional right-duty mix, not copied as GST into 51A.

questions.q: The ‘Ghadar Party’ was formed in:
options: North America by Indian emigrants (San Francisco etc.) before World War I
Dhaka in 1906 as the Muslim League
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Revolutionary diaspora; Komagata Maru is the linked current of that story.

questions.q: There has been a persistent deficit budget year after year. Which action can help reduce the deficit?
options: Revenue expenditure increase with no receipts
Raising tax revenue and/or cutting avoidable spending / better targeting of subsidies
Only printing notes with no fiscal plan
questions.solution: Correct option: B. FRBM logic: quality of spending + tax base. Monetising deficit has inflation costs.

questions.q: On which of the following can you find the Bureau of Energy Efficiency Star Label?
options: Selected appliances such as ACs, refrigerators, etc.
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Standards and labelling under the Energy Conservation Act; BEE is the statutory agency.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are coastal processes?
options: Longshore drift, wave erosion and beach deposition
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Class 11 geomorphology: destructive and constructive waves, spits, lagoons.

questions.q: Project Loon, sometimes in the news, was associated with:
questions.solution: Correct option: A. Digital divide / connectivity as GS-III. Treat company projects as application stories, not as current affairs forever.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct about the Lok Sabha?
options: Its maximum strength is fixed at 250 like Rajya Sabha
It is the House to which the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Article 75: collective responsibility to Lok Sabha. That is the core of the parliamentary executive.

questions.q: Banjaras during the medieval period were:
options: Trader-nomads who moved grain and goods with pack animals
questions.solution: Correct option: B. Themes in Indian History / NCERT: itinerant communities and the agrarian market.

papers.note: Official 2024 GS-I questions with model-answer skeletons.

questions.q: Underline the changes in the field of society and economy from the Rig Vedic to the later Vedic period.
questions.solution: Intro: pastoral janas → agrarian janapadas. Body: (i) iron, settled agriculture, land as wealth; (ii) varna crystallises, gotra, patriarchal household; (iii) rituals (srauta) and brahmana dominance; (iv) eastward shift to Ganga. Bihar hook: later Vedic sets the stage for mahajanapadas/Magadha. Close: continuity of cattle prestige with a new agrarian surplus.

questions.q: Estimate the contribution of Pallavas of Kanchi for the development of art and literature of South India.
questions.solution: Mandapa and ratha experiments at Mahabalipuram; structural Shore Temple; Sanskrit and Tamil patronage (Mahendravarman as playwright). They are the bridge to Chola bronze-and-temple urbanism. Mention Chinese/SE Asian contacts lightly.

questions.q: What were the events that led to the Quit India Movement? Point out its results.
questions.solution: Cripps failure, wartime inflation, Japanese threat, Gandhi’s ‘Do or Die’. 8 August 1942; mass upsurge, parallel governments, brutal suppression. Results: Congress banned, leaders jailed, but British legitimacy cracked; 1946 elections and Cabinet Mission follow. Bihar: 1942 underground activity.

questions.q: What is sea surface temperature rise? How does it affect the formation of tropical cyclones?
questions.solution: SST is the skin temperature of the ocean mixed layer. Cyclones need ~26.5°C, low shear, Coriolis. Warmer SST → more latent heat, possibly higher intensity and rapid intensification; genesis location may shift. Bay of Bengal is India’s risk theatre.

questions.q: Why do large cities tend to attract more migrants than smaller towns? Discuss in the light of conditions in developing countries.
questions.solution: Agglomeration: jobs, education, hospitals, networks, informal entry. Cumulative causation (Myrdal). Push: agrarian distress. Developing-country flavour: informal housing, gig work, female independent migration. Policy: small-town employment, portable social security.

questions.q: What is the phenomenon of ‘cloudbursts’? Explain.
questions.solution: Very high rainfall intensity over a small area/short time, often orographic + unstable moist air. Himalayan valleys: flash floods, landslides. Early warning, land-use, and not treating it as a ‘mystery’.

questions.q: What is the concept of a ‘demographic winter’? Is the world moving towards such a situation? Elaborate.
questions.solution: Prolonged below-replacement fertility, ageing, shrinking workforce. East Asia/Europe yes; Africa/parts of South Asia no. India is heterogeneous: south ageing faster than Bihar-UP. Policy: skills, care economy, not panic natalism alone.

questions.q: Distinguish between gender equality, gender equity and women’s empowerment. Why is it important to take gender concerns into account in programme design?
questions.solution: Equality: same treatment. Equity: fair treatment recognising disadvantage. Empowerment: agency over resources and body. Gender-blind schemes miss unpaid care, safety, land titles. Use sex-disaggregated data and GRB.

questions.q: “Though the great Cholas are no more yet their name is still remembered with great pride because of their highest achievements in the domain of art and architecture.” Comment.
questions.solution: Brihadisvara, Gangaikondacholapuram, bronze Nataraja, temple as economic unit, naval SE Asia. Art is political theology plus artisan guilds. Close with living ritual at Thanjavur.

questions.q: How far is it correct to say that the First World War was fought essentially for the preservation of balance of power?
questions.solution: Partly: alliance rigidity, naval race, Balkans. Also imperial markets, nationalism, blank cheque. India: men and material, Home Rule, 1919 reforms. Do not reduce to a single cause.

questions.q: How far was the Industrial Revolution in England responsible for the decline of handicrafts and cottage industries in India?
questions.solution: Machine cloth + tariffs + railways as one-way trade; deindustrialisation debate (Nationalists vs Morris). Not the only cause: Company weavers’ coercion earlier. Link to GS-III MSME today.

questions.q: The groundwater potential of the Gangetic valley is on a serious decline. How may it affect the food security of India?
questions.solution: Tube-well revolution, rice-wheat, electricity subsidy. Falling water tables → cost, arsenic/fluoride, rabi risk. Food security is availability + access + nutrition. Solutions: cropping shift, MIS, power reforms, Atal Bhujal flavour.

papers.note: Official 2024 GS-II questions with model-answer skeletons.

questions.q: Examine the need for electoral reforms as suggested by various committees with particular reference to “one nation – one election”.
questions.solution: Committees: Tarkunde, Dinesh Goswami, Indrajit Gupta, Law Commission, EC proposals (criminalisation, funding). ONOP: cost, policy paralysis vs federal terms, constitutional amendments, Law Commission caution. Balanced close.

questions.q: Explain and distinguish between Lok Adalats and Arbitration Tribunals. Whether they entertain civil as well as criminal cases?
questions.solution: Lok Adalat: Legal Services Authorities Act, conciliation, award = decree, compoundable criminal matters. Arbitration: Arbitration Act, private, contractual, civil/commercial — not criminal prosecution. Speed vs natural justice.

questions.q: “The growth of cabinet system has practically resulted in the marginalisation of the parliamentary supremacy.” Elucidate.
questions.solution: Collective responsibility + majority → executive dominates legislative time. Anti-defection, ordinance, money bill route. Counter: committees, Rajya Sabha, judicial review. Reform: more committee hours.

questions.q: “The duty of the CAG is not merely to ensure the legality of expenditure but also its propriety.” Comment.
questions.solution: Audit of regularity vs propriety/performance. 2nd ARC, CAG reports as PAC fuel. Limits: post-facto, not policy veto. Examples: defence, welfare leakage.

questions.q: Analyse the role of local bodies in good governance at local level and the pros and cons of merging rural local bodies with urban local bodies.
questions.solution: 73/74: proximity, 11th/12th Schedules. Merger: census towns, peri-urban services vs Gram Sabha identity, fiscal transfers. Bihar: rapidly urbanising blocks.

questions.q: Critically analyse India’s relations with the Central Asian Republics.
questions.solution: Connect Central Asia policy, INSTC, Chabahar, SCO, energy, extremism. Limits: geography, Pakistan/Afghanistan, China. Concrete projects over communiqués.

questions.q: What are the aims of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024? Are University/State Board exams covered?
questions.solution: Paper leaks as a governance crisis (Bihar relevance). Act targets organised cheating in notified public exams. State boards/universities need notification/separate law — do not assume automatic coverage. Implementation + policing capacity.

questions.q: Right to privacy is intrinsic to Article 21. Discuss DNA testing of a child in the womb to establish paternity.
questions.solution: Puttaswamy tests: legality, legitimate aim, proportionality. Foetal DNA: bodily autonomy of woman, best interests of child, dignity. Courts allow only when eminent need, not as a fishing enquiry.

questions.q: What changes has the Union recently introduced in Centre–State relations? Suggest measures to build trust.
questions.solution: GST, CSS, Governors, tax devolution, cesses, disaster funds. Measures: more tax devolution, fewer cesses, Inter-State Council, cooperative agencies, respect for elected state governments. Neutral tone.

questions.q: Explain the growth of PIL. Has the Indian Supreme Court become the world’s most powerful judiciary?
questions.solution: Hussainara, Judges Transfer, epistolary jurisdiction, Article 21 expansion. Power: review of constitutional amendments, collegium, continuing mandamus. Limits: docket, enforcement, democratic critique of overreach.

papers.note: Official 2024 GS-III themes with model-answer skeletons.

questions.q: Examine the pattern of public expenditure on social services in the post-reforms period. Has it served inclusive growth?
questions.solution: 1991: fiscal squeeze then CSS expansion (education, health, NREGA, DBT). Outcomes: literacy/health gains with quality and jobless-growth gaps. Inclusive growth = jobs + human capital + regions. Cite Survey ratios, not slogans.

questions.q: What are the causes of persistent high food inflation in India? Comment on RBI monetary policy effectiveness against it.
questions.solution: Supply: weather, proteins, logistics, MSP-procurement, global oils. Demand: rural wages. Repo is a blunt tool for vegetable shocks; buffers, imports, operation greens. MPC still anchors expectations.

questions.q: Explain the role of millets for health and nutritional security in India.
questions.solution: Climate-smart, micronutrients, rainfed Bihar plateau fringe/Jharkhand. IYM 2023. Constraints: processing, taste, procurement. Link PDS diversification and anaemia.

questions.q: What technology is used for electronic toll collection on highways? Advantages, limits, hazards?
questions.solution: FASTag/RFID. Time, fuel, leak-proof toll. Limits: KYC, blacklisting, privacy, local employment at plazas. Cyber and data localisation as hazards.

questions.q: Industrial pollution of rivers is a significant issue. Discuss mitigation and government initiatives.
questions.solution: Effluent standards, CETP, CPCB/SPCB, NGT, Namami Gange, EPR. Enforcement gap. Bihar: Ganga stretches, tanneries/distilleries upstream. Combine law + financing + real-time monitoring.

questions.q: Explain how narco-terrorism has emerged as a threat. Suggest measures.
questions.solution: Golden Crescent/Triangle, drones, darknet, terror finance. Measures: NCB, FATF-style AML, border tech, demand-side health, coastal/airport scanning. Rights-compliant policing.

questions.q: Discuss disaster resilience. Mention elements of a resilience framework.
questions.solution: Sendai: understand risk, strengthen governance, invest, build back better. Structural vs non-structural. Bihar floods: embankment limits, early warning, shelters, insurance.

questions.q: The application of AI as a dependable input for administrative decisions is debatable. Critically examine from an ethical point of view.
questions.solution: Pros: speed, pattern detection, leak-proof targeting. Cons: bias, opacity, accountability gap, exclusion errors. Ethical tests: fairness, explainability, human-in-loop, appeal. Example: welfare lists, policing.

questions.q: Global warming as an outcome of human greed — how do you restore equilibrium between society and environment?
questions.solution: Trusteeship, inter-generational equity, polluter pays, sufficiency. Policy: carbon price, just transition, adaptation in Bihar flood–heat geography. Personal: consumption ethic without sermonising.

questions.q: “The concept of just and unjust is contextual… law should be constantly under scrutiny.” Examine.
questions.solution: Legal positivism vs natural justice. Constitutional morality (Ambedkar), basic structure, judicial review. Examples: emergency excesses, privacy, same-sex dignity. Scrutiny ≠ anarchy; it is democratic constitutionalism.

questions.q: A district officer must target flood relief when local elites capture lists. Outline the ethical decision process.
questions.solution: Facts → stakeholders (victims, panchayat, contractors, media) → options (do nothing, use SECC/GIS, social audit, FIR) → public interest + compassion + rule of law → communicate and monitor. Avoid partisanship.

questions.q: Explain the role of geographical factors towards the development of Ancient India.
questions.solution: Monsoon agriculture, Himalaya–Ocean bounds, passes, rivers (Saraswati debate as geography not myth), coasts for trade. Magadha: iron, forests, Ganga–Son. Geography is possibility, not destiny.

questions.q: What was the difference between Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore in their approach towards education and nationalism?
questions.solution: Gandhi: Nai Talim, vernacular, swaraj as self-rule of the self. Tagore: Visva-Bharati, world culture, critique of narrow nationalism. Both anti-colonial, different cosmopolitanisms.

questions.q: Why is caste identity in India both fluid and durable? Discuss.
questions.solution: Sanskritisation, politics, urban jobs vs endogamy, census/Mandal. Durable because it organises marriage and networks; fluid at the edges of class and region.

questions.q: “Constitutionally guaranteed judicial independence is a prerequisite of democracy.” Discuss.
questions.solution: Security of tenure, salaries, contempt, judicial review. Collegium vs NJAC. Independence is for the Constitution, not for the corporation of judges. Accountability via reasoned orders and integrity.

questions.q: The expansion and strengthening of NATO and a stronger US-Europe strategic partnership faces new challenges due to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Comment.
questions.solution: NATO rediscovery, energy shock, Global South unease, India’s strategic autonomy, food/fertiliser. Do not write a NATO press release; write India’s interest.

questions.q: Faster economic growth requires increased share of the manufacturing sector in GDP, particularly of MSMEs. Comment on the present policies.
questions.solution: Premature deindustrialisation risk, PLI, logistics, credit, labour. MSME: delayed payments, formalisation via GST/UPI. Jobs are the test.

questions.q: What are the internal security challenges being faced by India? Give out the role of Central and State agencies.
questions.solution: LWE, NE insurgency, terror, cyber, narcotics, communal. Federal policing: State list vs central forces, NIA, NATGRID flavour. Coordination and rights.

questions.q: What do you understand by ‘moral integrity’ and ‘professional efficiency’ in the context of corporate governance? Illustrate.
questions.solution: Integrity: honest reporting, related-party restraint. Efficiency: fiduciary duty to create value lawfully. Satyam vs well-run PSU/private boards. SEBI LODR as the hard shell of ethics.

questions.q: How will you explain that medieval Indian temple sculptures represent the social life of those days?
questions.solution: Donors, dancers, warriors, erotic mithuna, caste guilds on walls. Temple as a social document, not only a deity. Compare Khajuraho, Konark, Hoysala.

questions.q: Discuss the meaning of colour-coded weather warnings for cyclone prone areas given by IMD.
questions.solution: Green/yellow/orange/red: no action → watch → be prepared → take action. Link NDMA, last-mile in Odisha vs Bihar thunderstorms. Communication ethics: no panic, no complacency.

questions.q: The Attorney-General is the chief legal adviser of the Government. Discuss his roles and limitations.
questions.solution: Article 76, right of audience, aid and advice flavour but not a minister. Cannot vote in Parliament. Independence vs being the government’s lawyer — tension in politically charged references.

questions.q: Do you think that BIMSTEC is a parallel organisation like the SAARC? What are the popular theories about BIMSTEC?
questions.solution: BIMSTEC: Bay of Bengal, energy, connectivity, security — India can work without a SAARC veto. Not a clone; a pragmatic mini-lateral. Delivery on projects is the test.

questions.q: Trace the rise and growth of socio-religious reform movements with special reference to Young Bengal.
questions.solution: Derozio, rationalism, women’s education, against orthodoxy. Limits: elite, urban. Place beside Brahmo, Aligarh, Jyotiba Phule.

questions.q: Differentiate the causes of landslides in the Himalayan region and Western Ghats.
questions.solution: Himalaya: young fold, earthquakes, rain, road cutting, dams. Ghats: laterite, rainfall, plantation, quarrying. Common: land-use. NDMA guidelines.

questions.q: ‘Constitutional Morality’ is rooted in the Constitution itself and is to be found in the Preamble, the FRs and DPSPs. Comment.
questions.solution: Ambedkar: not public morality of the crowd. Examples: privacy, inclusion, anti-untouchability. Courts use it; critique: judicial subjectivity. Anchor in text.

questions.q: Has digitalization empowered the Indian citizen? Discuss.
questions.solution: DBT, UPI, RTI online, CoWIN. Exclusion: authentication failures, connectivity, literacy. Empowerment needs grievance redress, not only apps.

questions.q: Persian literary sources of medieval India reflect the spirit of the age. Comment.
questions.solution: Court chronicles (Barani, Abul Fazl) as ideology; travelogues; sufi tazkiras. Bias of patronage. Use alongside inscriptions and architecture.

questions.q: Do you agree that regionalism in India appears to be a consequence of rising cultural assertiveness? Discuss.
questions.solution: Language, statehood, development lag, political mobilisation. Not only culture: fiscal federalism and migration (Bihar). Accommodation via States Reorganisation and 73rd.

questions.q: Rajya Sabha has been transformed from a ‘useless stepney tyre’ to an indispensably important institution. Comment.
questions.solution: Federal second chamber, revision, 249/312, experienced members. Still: money bill disputes, disruptions. Strengthen committees rather than abolish.

questions.q: ‘Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad)’ is transforming itself into a trade block from a military alliance, in present times. Discuss.
questions.solution: Quad is not NATO. Vaccines, infrastructure, maritime domain awareness, critical tech. India keeps strategic autonomy and Russia/China realities. Call it a coalition of interests.

questions.q: Highlight the Central Asian and Greco-Bactrian elements in the Gandhara art.
questions.solution: Hellenistic drapery, Buddha as Apollo-like, schist, narrative Jatakas. Syncretic Silk Road. Contrast Mathura red sandstone.

questions.q: Explain how the foundations of the modern world were laid by the American and French Revolutions.
questions.solution: Rights, constitution, nation, citizen. Limits: slavery, colonial France. India: liberal vocabulary of Moderates; later mass politics exceeds it.

questions.q: Do you think the Constitution of India does not accept the principle of strict separation of powers? Discuss.
questions.solution: Functional overlap: ordinance, delegated legislation, judicial review, parliamentary privileges. Checks, not Chinese walls. Contrast US. Basic structure still protects each organ’s core.

questions.q: ‘The time has come for India and Japan to build a strong contemporary relationship.’ In the light of this, discuss economic, cultural and defence aspects.
questions.solution: Act East, corridors, bullet train flavour, Quad, defence logistics. Culture: Buddhism. Caveats: trade imbalance, China hedging.

questions.q: Safeguarding the Indian art heritage is the need of the moment. Discuss.
questions.solution: Thefts, pollution, urbanisation, poor documentation. ASI, AMASR, UNESCO, community arts (Madhubani). Heritage as livelihood, not only monuments.

questions.q: ‘Caste system is assuming new identities and associational forms. Hence, the caste system cannot be eradicated in India.’ Comment.
questions.solution: From ritual hierarchy to political blocs and matrimonial markets. Law (17, PoA) plus economy plus education. Eradication is a horizon; reduction of humiliation is the metric.

questions.q: In the light of recent controversy regarding the use of Electronic Voting Machines (EVM), what are the challenges before the Election Commission?
questions.solution: Trust is the product. VVPAT, mock polls, audits, communication. Challenge: rumour vs evidence. EC independence and logistics in heat/floods.

questions.q: E-governance is not just about routine application of digital technology; it is as much about interactions for transparency. Comment.
questions.solution: G2C/G2G, interactive service model, RTI + dashboards, social audit. Failure modes: dashboards without grievance. Bihar service delivery examples, non-partisan.
